assumptions: The directed edges in state_graph.json define dependency flow from prerequisite artifact to dependent artifact.
A node becomes STALE when any upstream dependency changes, so all graph descendants of the changed node are stale.
The restart stage labels provided in changes.json are the target policy stages to verify against graph-derived stale sets.

baseline.description: Manual descendant tracing directly from each changed node along outgoing edges, then comparing the reached nodes with expected_stale and restart fields.
evidence: Manual tracing from input reaches audit -> model -> run-1 -> final-run-1 -> result-table -> evidence-package.
Manual tracing from config reaches run-1 -> final-run-1 -> result-table -> evidence-package.
Manual tracing from final-run-1 reaches result-table -> evidence-package.
baseline.result: All three simulated changes matched their expected stale descendants and restart stages.

candidate_models: Baseline candidate: manual graph walk from each changed node to enumerate descendants and compare with changes.json.
Candidate 2: executable breadth-first traversal over the adjacency list to compute descendants for each change and verify equality with expected_stale.
Candidate 3 rejected: infer stale nodes only from stage names in restart labels; rejected because labels alone cannot recover full descendant sets or verify graph consistency.
claims: Verified: all three simulated changes have expected_stale sets consistent with descendant-based stale propagation on the provided graph.
Verified: the earliest restart stages in changes.json are consistent with the changed nodes and their downstream dependencies.
Inferred from the dependency policy and prompt wording: stale descendants must preserve history through append/supersede behavior rather than manual report repair.
Inferred from the same policy: stale paper or evidence handoff must be blocked until the earliest affected stage and all downstream artifacts are regenerated.
code_artifacts: No files were created or edited.
An inline python3 breadth-first traversal script was executed in the shell to verify descendant sets against changes.json.
data_findings: state_graph.json defines nodes input, audit, model, config, run-1, final-run-1, result-table, and evidence-package.
Graph edges show two parents for run-1: model and config.
CHANGE-INPUT changes input; its descendants are audit, model, run-1, final-run-1, result-table, and evidence-package.
CHANGE-CONFIG changes config; its descendants are run-1, final-run-1, result-table, and evidence-package.
CHANGE-FINAL changes final-run-1; its descendants are result-table and evidence-package.
Each expected_stale list in changes.json matches the graph-derived descendant set for its changed node.
Each restart label in changes.json matches the earliest affected stage implied by the changed node: data audit for input, run execution for config, and downstream result generation for final-run-1.
experiment_design: Use two structurally distinct approaches: manual tracing baseline and executable graph traversal candidate.
Start with a minimal sanity case on the input node before trusting the executable traversal for all records.
Then evaluate every change record independently and compare computed descendants and restart stage expectations with the provided data.
falsification_tests: If any reachable descendant had been missing from an expected_stale list, the selected model would have flagged the change record inconsistent.
If a restart label had pointed later than the earliest affected stage, the record would fail the restart-stage check.
If the graph had contained an alternate path that manual tracing missed, disagreement between baseline and executable traversal would have falsified the manual result.

constraints: Preserve the append/supersede history implication by treating stale descendants as requiring regeneration instead of manual overwrite.
Fail closed when evidence for freshness is absent; stale downstream artifacts cannot be handed off as current.
Do not treat downstream prose or report edits as a valid substitute for rerunning the earliest affected stage.
notes: The key dependency rule is descendant closure: every downstream reachable artifact from a changed node is stale.
Because result-table and evidence-package are derived artifacts, they remain stale until regenerated from the earliest affected upstream stage.
No change record justifies marking any artifact FINAL; the task requires freshness analysis only.
formalization.objective: Verify whether each simulated change record is consistent with dependency-driven stale propagation and earliest restart staging.
parameters: Stage labels data audit, run execution, and downstream result generation from changes.json.
units: Graph entities are discrete artifact/stage nodes.
Restart output is a categorical stage label.
variables: G = directed graph induced by state_graph.json edges.
c = changed node for a simulated change record.
Desc(c) = all nodes reachable from c by one or more outgoing edges.
